segments.text: Bakit kailangan ng Ombudsman ng 54 million na confidential funds?

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: pero pinapa-realign in other items, no.

segments.speaker: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin C. Remulla
segments.text: Your Honor, the office of the ombudsman can dismiss barangay captains who do not do their job.

segments.speaker: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin C. Remulla
segments.text: And I think all we need is a substantiated complaint, a complaint that people will stand up to,

segments.speaker: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin C. Remulla
segments.text: will try to prove to us so that we can utilize this power given to us by the law.

segments.speaker: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin C. Remulla
segments.text: And it's just something, it's just probably unfortunate that I have to mention this.

segments.speaker: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin C. Remulla
segments.text: Many of those that we have dismissed in the office of the ombudsman institutionally,

segments.speaker: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin C. Remulla
segments.text: in many cases, these are talking about many, many cases, were reversed by the Court of Appeals.

segments.speaker: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin C. Remulla
segments.text: That is a trend, Your Honor, that's known to the whole office of the ombudsman.

segments.speaker: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin C. Remulla

segments.speaker: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin C. Remulla
segments.text: I told him about this problem that we have.

segments.speaker: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin C. Remulla
segments.text: Because institutionally, it's very discouraging to be conducting all of these activities

segments.text: only to be reversed by the Court of Appeals decision that came out of nowhere.

segments.speaker: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin C. Remulla
segments.text: I mean, sometimes we feel that way.

segments.text: And I was actually confronted with that problem as Secretary of Justice

segments.speaker: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin C. Remulla
segments.text: There was somebody dismissed by the office of the ombudsman

segments.speaker: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin C. Remulla
segments.text: Which decision was reversed by the Court of Appeals

segments.speaker: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin C. Remulla
segments.text: and was trying to get back to his office in the NBI.

segments.speaker: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin C. Remulla
segments.text: And I could not honor that kind of logic

segments.speaker: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin C. Remulla
segments.text: because he had been dismissed already.

segments.speaker: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin C. Remulla
segments.text: And if you will be reversed in your dismissal,

segments.speaker: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin C. Remulla
segments.text: what then is the power given to us?

segments.speaker: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin C. Remulla
segments.text: If that will be the case.

segments.speaker: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin C. Remulla
segments.text: So, that's one of the dilemmas that we face with the judiciary, Your Honor.

segments.text: I'm sorry to say, but as a lawyer,

segments.speaker: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin C. Remulla
segments.text: it's not really common for lawyers to complain about the courts.

segments.speaker: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin C. Remulla
segments.text: But sometimes we just have to raise that issue already

segments.speaker: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin C. Remulla
segments.text: because it can be the biggest elephant in the room within our justice system.

segments.speaker: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin C. Remulla
segments.text: If you talk about foreign investment,

segments.text: we have a problem with foreign investment

segments.speaker: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin C. Remulla
segments.text: because there's no certainty that the rules will apply to the judiciary.

segments.speaker: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin C. Remulla
segments.text: It's something that has to be dealt with face-to-face by our people

segments.speaker: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin C. Remulla
segments.text: and by the legislators, by all of us.

segments.speaker: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin C. Remulla
segments.text: It's the biggest elephant in the room for this country.

segments.speaker: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin C. Remulla
segments.text: The judiciary has to be examined closely by everybody in government

segments.speaker: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin C. Remulla

segments.text: So rest assured that the Senate, under the leadership of the Senate President, will be foursquare behind the efforts of the Ombudsman.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Yes, before the Senate President, I would like to acknowledge also the presence of our Blue Ribbon Chair, Senator Erwin Tulfo.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Thank you, sir, for joining us.

segments.speaker: Senator Sherwin "Win" T. Gatchalian
segments.text: Mr. Chairman, just a brief intervention lang.

segments.speaker: Senator Sherwin "Win" T. Gatchalian
segments.text: I was looking at itong corruption index scores natin, corruption perception index.

segments.speaker: Senator Sherwin "Win" T. Gatchalian
segments.text: And sad to say, in the last three years, bumagsak yung ating ranking, from 144, the lowest rank being the least corrupt.

segments.speaker: Senator Sherwin "Win" T. Gatchalian
segments.text: From 144 rank naging 120 rank na tayo.

segments.speaker: Senator Sherwin "Win" T. Gatchalian
segments.text: And we're now the third most corrupt in Southeast Asia, next to Myanmar and Cambodia, which are...

segments.speaker: Senator Sherwin "Win" T. Gatchalian
segments.text: alam naman natin, are junta states.

segments.speaker: Senator Sherwin "Win" T. Gatchalian
segments.text: So there is really a very big challenge for all of us to improve the perception of corruption in our country.

segments.speaker: Senator Sherwin "Win" T. Gatchalian
segments.text: In fact, one of the reasons bakit mahina ang peso, dahil walang demand sa peso.

segments.speaker: Senator Sherwin "Win" T. Gatchalian
segments.text: Kasama na dito rin itong, of course, ease of doing business and also the perception of corruption.

segments.speaker: Senator Sherwin "Win" T. Gatchalian
segments.text: So it's really a big challenge for all of us.

segments.speaker: Senator Sherwin "Win" T. Gatchalian
segments.text: And that is why I second the statement of Senator Lacson na

segments.speaker: Senator Sherwin "Win" T. Gatchalian
segments.text: whatever we can do to help the Ombudsman, even the judiciary, to fight corruption, we will do it.

segments.speaker: Senator Sherwin "Win" T. Gatchalian
segments.text: Because it affects our country, it affects our OFWs, it affects even the most ordinary Filipino.

segments.speaker: Senator Sherwin "Win" T. Gatchalian
segments.text: So kailangan talaga magtulong-tulong tayo diyan.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Our Blue Ribbon Chair is also here.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Senator Erwin Tulfo, you now have the floor.

segments.speaker: Senator Erwin Tulfo
segments.text: Anyway, I don't know, Mr. Chair, if this was already asked.

segments.speaker: Senator Erwin Tulfo
segments.text: Ito lang po nakita ko, napansin kanina dito.

segments.speaker: Senator Erwin Tulfo
segments.text: Itong total number of authorized positions, Mr. Chair.

segments.speaker: Senator Erwin Tulfo
segments.text: 2,439 po nire-request po ng authorized positions.

segments.speaker: Senator Erwin Tulfo
segments.text: Pero ang filled positions lamang ay 1,192.

segments.speaker: Senator Erwin Tulfo
segments.text: Dito po sa 2,439, Mr. Chair, Ombudsman, karamihan po ba nito ay mga investigators po ninyo?

segments.speaker: Senator Erwin Tulfo
segments.text: Sa anong mga positions po ito?

segments.speaker: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin C. Remulla
segments.text: We will need more lawyers and technical investigators, Your Honor.

segments.speaker: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin C. Remulla
segments.text: Engineers who can educate us about infrastructure fraud, infrastructure corruption.

segments.speaker: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin C. Remulla
segments.text: And other specialists, Your Honor, who are good at investigating different kinds of crimes, Your Honor.

segments.speaker: Senator Erwin Tulfo
segments.text: Hindi po ito yung basta-bastang mga contractual employees.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Yung tungkol sa Resident Ombudsman Program, what is the current status of the Resident Ombudsman Program,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: including the number of active resident ombudsmen, their deployment across agencies,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: and the key accomplishments or challenges encountered recently?

segments.speaker: Assistant Ombudsman Luis Gonzaga S. Bonoan, Jr.
segments.text: Your Honor, actually, during this administration, we have reactivated the Bureau of the Resident Ombudsman,

segments.speaker: Assistant Ombudsman Luis Gonzaga S. Bonoan, Jr.
Assistant Ombudsman Luis Gonzaga S. Bonoan, Jr.
Assistant Ombudsman Luis Gonzaga S. Bonoan, Jr.
segments.text: So, as of today, we have hired an additional 10 lawyers to complement our Bureau of Resident Ombudsman.

segments.speaker: Assistant Ombudsman Luis Gonzaga S. Bonoan, Jr.
segments.text: And we have plans, sir, after conducting the proper training, of fielding them out in different agencies,

segments.speaker: Assistant Ombudsman Luis Gonzaga S. Bonoan, Jr.
segments.text: particularly the high revenue generating agencies, sir, to investigate and collect complaints from therein.

segments.speaker: Assistant Ombudsman Luis Gonzaga S. Bonoan, Jr.
Assistant Ombudsman Luis Gonzaga S. Bonoan, Jr.
Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Anyway, before we close, if there are no more questions or queries from our colleagues.

segments.speaker: Senator Vicente C. Sotto III
segments.text: I move that we submit and approve the budget of the Ombudsman, together with the proposed amendments.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Since it has been moved by our Senate President Pro Tempore and seconded,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: the budget of the Office of the Ombudsman is now deemed submitted for the plenary's consideration,

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: subject to the discussion and submission of documents requested.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Thank you very much, gentlemen, Ombudsman, and to all the rest of the officials of the Office of the Ombudsman.
